_readme: All quantities are simulated. Every parameter carries a source and a 'verified' flag: true = checked against a cited source, false = an assumption to be validated (see plan section 11). Nothing here is real company or government data.

R-404A.source: EU F-gas Regulation 2024/573 Annex (IPCC AR4 values)

R-134a.source: EU F-gas Regulation 2024/573 Annex (IPCC AR4 values)

R-410A.source: EU F-gas Regulation 2024/573 Annex (IPCC AR4 values)

registry.source: Türkiye F-gas regulation (Resmî Gazete 32693, 2024-10-15): EKOMVET registration for equipment >= 5 tCO2e

medium_large_commercial.source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol.3 Ch.7 Table 7.9 via Climate Action Reserve (2018): medium/large commercial 10–35 %/yr

standalone_commercial.source: IPCC 2006 GL Table 7.9 via ACR peer review (2023): stand-alone 0.2–6 kg, 1–15 %/yr

chiller.source: IPCC 2006 GL Table 7.9 via Climate Action Reserve (2018): chillers 2–15 %/yr

split_ac.source: Assumed (IPCC residential/commercial AC 1–10 %/yr could not be confirmed)

service._maintenanceReadme: Who tops units up. Small units that are Tier A (>= 5 tCO2e) are leak-checked by law and so reach end of life fuller than the generic IPCC small-unit default (0-80 %): a stated modelling choice. Tier A units (>= 5 tCO2e) must be leak-checked periodically (EU Reg. 2024/573 Art. 5; Turkiye's F-gas regulation registers the same units in EKOMVET), so they are refilled when a check finds them low. Tier B units have no leak-check obligation: they are refilled only when they stop cooling. End-of-life remaining charge is NOT drawn from IPCC Table 7.9; it emerges from this behaviour and is compared with the Table 7.9 ranges (fleet.categories.*.ipccEolRemaining) as a calibration check.
service.leakCheckSource: EU Reg. 2024/573 Art. 5(3) frequencies for units without leak detection: 5-50 t every 12 months, 50-500 t every 6 months, >= 500 t every 3 months (as recalled; check the text)
service.tierBRepairSource: Assumption, calibrated: a small unit is noticed when it stops cooling (below ~30 % of its charge); most are replaced rather than repaired. 2 % a month puts ~80 % of Tier B end-of-life remaining charges inside the IPCC Table 7.9 range of 0-80 % (seeds 1-5; medians 0.41 stand-alone, 0.55 split AC). With 20 % a month only ~55 % were inside. The ~20 % outside are mainly split ACs at the bottom of their unconfirmed 1-10 %/yr leak band.
service.source: Assumption: technicians top up when a leak check finds the charge 15 % low
service.companySizeReadme: Service companies differ in size: each unit picks its service company with these relative weights. Assumption, not verified.
service.companyLeakFactorReadme: Honest maintenance quality differs: each service company's units leak at the drawn category rate times this factor (better maintenance, less leakage). Assumption, not verified.

endOfLife.recoveryRateSource: Japan MOE, OEWG48 side-event deck (Jul 2026): 5,188 t recovered of 12,011 t remaining at disposal in 2024

reclaim._readme: Each honest reclaimer has its own plant efficiency: a yield centre drawn once, then batch yields within +/- the half-width. Some honest plants are therefore naturally high-yield.

destruction.source: Isometric HFC & ODS Recovery and Destruction Protocol v1.0: DRE >= 99.99 %

observationNoise._readme: Honest paperwork is not perfectly aligned with the ledger: invoice weights are rounded/estimated and invoices are dated a few days before or after the shipment. Without this, any invoice/ledger gap would be fraud by construction.

rules._readme: Mirror of the on-chain parameters. Must match KigaliLedger / EquipmentRegistry defaults.

actors._ownersReadme: Equipment owners co-sign every recovery from their Tier A units (supermarket chains, building operators). Take-back points own scrapped Tier B units. Verifiers sign destruction certificates.

fraud._readme: Injected scenarios with ground-truth labels, used only to evaluate the AI modules. Patterns follow fraud modes documented by EIA (2026); magnitudes are assumptions.

offLedgerTopUps._readme: Service companies that top units up with smuggled gas off the ledger. Naive ones record 20 % of top-ups and buy the smuggled gas on invoices. Adaptive ones record just enough that every unit's ledger leakage sits between its category's IPCC minimum and midpoint, and pay cash for smuggled gas (no invoice).

distributorOverselling._readme: Distributors that sell smuggled gas off the ledger. The naive one bills it on separate invoices. The adaptive one knows the 5 % weight tolerance: it delivers smuggled gas together with legitimate shipments and pads those invoices by at most 4 % each, and keeps the total under 2 % of its ledger sales.

phantomTierB._readme: Fake small units 'recovered' with smuggled virgin gas. Needs a colluding take-back point to co-sign as owner; that take-back point also does ordinary business. The first company is naive (1-4 fake units a month, ~the full model charge); the second adapts: it books one fake unit in about 15 % of months (as many as a large honest company scraps) at an honest-looking share of the model charge (small units reach end of life far from full: IPCC Table 7.9 gives 0-80 % remaining).

inflatedYield._readme: Reclaimers that blend virgin gas into 'reclaimed' output. The naive one books 93-98 % yields and sometimes tries to exceed the 98 % ceiling (rejected by R4); the adaptive one keeps its own plant's spread and only shifts its centre up by a few points, so it looks like an efficient honest plant and never hits the ceiling.

unconsentedRecovery._readme: Off-ledger services book smuggled gas as recovered from someone else's unit, signing the consent with their own key (rejected: NotUnitOwner).

cylinderReuse._readme: A phantom service books a recovery into a cylinder that still backs an open lot (rejected: CylinderInUse).

selfCertifiedDestruction._readme: A facility signs its own destruction certificate (rejected: NotVerifier).

paddedRecovery._readme: A service company and a colluding owner book more than the unit can hold: either one recovery above one charge, or (split padding) a full charge from a unit already partly recovered with no recorded recharge. Both pass the lifetime cap (charge + top-ups); the booked-content rule rejects them (RecoveryExceedsContent). Drawn from a separate random stream so the rest of the run is unchanged; each kind is tried at this rate.
